pageDescription: Information about regulatory bodies overseeing futures trading and financial system stability in Indonesia
profile_description: Below are the key regulatory authorities overseeing the futures trading industry and the broader financial sector in Indonesia. Each institution plays a strategic role in maintaining market stability, transparency, and integrity.

bappebti.title: COMMODITY FUTURES TRADING REGULATORY AGENCY (BAPPEBTI)
bappebti.description: BAPPEBTI is a government institution under the Ministry of Trade mandated to ensure that the commodity futures trading industry operates in an orderly, transparent, and secure manner. Through strict regulation and supervision, BAPPEBTI helps maintain public trust and market integrity so that all futures transactions in Indonesia comply with applicable rules and standards.

bbj.title: FINANCIAL SERVICES AUTHORITY (OJK)
bbj.description: The Financial Services Authority (OJK) is an independent state institution responsible for implementing an integrated regulatory and supervisory system for all activities in the financial services sector. OJK ensures that the financial industry operates in a transparent, fair, and stable manner, protecting consumer interests while supporting sustainable national economic growth.

kbi.title: BANK INDONESIA (BI)
kbi.description: Bank Indonesia is the central bank of the Republic of Indonesia, mandated primarily to maintain the stability of the rupiah. Through monetary policy, a reliable payment system, and macroprudential supervision, Bank Indonesia plays a strategic role in safeguarding economic stability and supporting a strong and resilient national financial system.

sitna.title: NATIONAL TRANSACTION INFORMATION SYSTEM (SITNA)
sitna.description: The National Transaction Information System (SITNA) is an electronic system established by BAPPEBTI to record and report all commodity futures trading transactions carried out by Futures Exchanges, Clearing Houses, and Futures Brokers in Indonesia. SITNA is designed to enhance transparency, efficiency, and supervisory capabilities in the futures market, as well as to protect the interests of investors.
